title: Sequence-consistency canary: interleaved streaming + function-call regression harness and golden corpus
creator: Lena Patel
description:
Objective: Build a repeatable canary + regression harness that validates sequence-level consistency across interleaved streaming payloads and function/tool calls for text generation and structured output APIs. This ticket covers corpus creation (golden prompts that exercise partial message fragments, mid-stream function calls, multi-tool interactions, and KV-cache warm/cold transitions), an executor that replays deterministic event streams, and CI integration with job matrix shards for runtime/kernel variants.

Why: Recent incidents where chunk boundaries or function-call boundaries caused differing outputs across runtime kernels and quantization profiles led to customer regressions. We need an automated, runnable canary that surface regressions quickly and can be gated in PRs and mainline CI.

Scope & Deliverables:
- Golden prompt corpus (200 curated scenarios) annotated with expected sequence-level fingerprints and function-call JSON assertions. Corpus includes: prefix-truncation cases, interleaved tool call pairs, streaming fragment reassembly cases, out-of-order partial token deliveries, and KV cache boundary stress tests.
- Canary executor: replays streams (token fragments + event markers) against target model endpoints (hosted / dedicated / private) and captures full event logs and final assembled outputs. Supports simulated tool stubs and verifies structured output schemas.
- Contract checks: token-by-token stream comparison, JSON schema validation for function calls, and KV-cache state assertions (cache hits/misses at specific offsets).
- CI integration: GitHub Actions matrix to run fast smoke shard on PRs (10s of scenarios) and nightly full-run across kernel variants (cuda-ops, quantized-fp16, bfloat) and model families.
- Canary dashboard: lightweight SLO + failure classification page with links to artifacts and rerun buttons.

Acceptance criteria:
- Corpus stored at s3://redwood-ci/goldens/sequence-consistency-v1 and has metadata file with scenario IDs and expected fingerprints.
- Executor binary runs locally and in CI; test run against a known-good runtime returns 0 failures for baseline scenarios.
- PRs that touch serving/runtime or serializer code trigger PR-smoke and block merge on new failures (configurable guard).
- Alerts created in PagerDuty for nightly regression spikes above threshold (10 failing scenarios).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement model-diff visualization or automated root-cause attribution — those are follow-ups.

Tradeoffs and design notes:
- We will use a lightweight deterministic stub for tool behavior rather than spinning full external services to keep runs fast; a separate integration lane will exist for end-to-end tool integration tests.
- Prefer event-replay approach (exact token fragments and event timing) to fuzz-first initially; fuzz harness is planned later (ENG-64731).

Runbook / How to run locally:
1) Checkout repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/sequence-canary.git
2) aws s3 sync s3://redwood-ci/goldens/sequence-consistency-v1 ./goldens
3) ./canary_runner --scenario ./goldens/SCN-0001.json --endpoint http://localhost:8080 --tool-stub ./stubs/basic_tool.json

Metrics to track:
- nightly_failure_count, pr_smoke_failure_rate, mean_time_to_detect_regression, median_runtime_seconds_per-scenario

Release and rollout plan:
- Merge canary executor and corpus in runtime-1.20 branch behind feature flag; enable PR-smoke for serving/runtime changes in 2 weeks; enable nightly full run and paging after successful 2-week stabilization window.
